methods.name: Peer-Median

data.narrative:
Panthalassa is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Garth Sheldon-Coulson and Brian Moffat, having raised $140M+ to date. The valuation analysis triangulates across a peer universe of 9 private and 1 public comparables in the climate and energy sector, including later-stage peers KoBold Metals ($3.0B Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B Series C), and Amogy ($700M Series C).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $140M total capital raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B to subsequent-stage transitions, yielding $266M. Peer-median analysis anchors to the median valuation of three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables at $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $226M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $633M. The stage-progression method pulls toward the lower end, reflecting Panthalassa's earlier stage relative to the peer sample. The peer-median method reflects later-stage comparable valuations and introduces material dispersion—the $3.0B KoBold valuation significantly widens the upper bound. Key uncertainties include the timing and magnitude of Panthalassa's progression relative to peer trajectories, and whether the Series C peer set accurately reflects fair value for a Series B company in this rapidly evolving sector.
